verdict_reason: failing G3 criteria: contact_occurred, hand_world_pose_deviation_within_cap -- see retarget_qa.json

blocker.what: dual-hand W6a scene, single-hand-input mode (right hand executes the retargeted clip, left hand frozen at its reset pose): the base solve and the constrained solve solved -- the commanded hand sits 0.03 mm short of the box at the closest fingertip with 4 of four tips inside the grasp radius and 48.0 mm of palm-plate clearance -- but the executed replay falls short of the frozen G3 contract on three gates. (1) The physics holds the palm 193 mm away from the pose it is commanded (cap 40 mm): the servos do not track the solved pose in the world. (2) No finger/palm-vs-box contact occurs in any frame: the clip closes to a 0.03 mm gap and the position servos stop there, so the contact criterion is unproven on this scene rather than satisfied by a palm resting on the box, as on the superseded single-hand scene. (3) Three finger joints (the joints listed in servo_winding_tolerance.joints_with_excursion) sit up to a few mrad past jnt_range at the commanded boundary for up to 14 consecutive frames with a mN*m torque imbalance -- sub-tolerance boundary dust that fails the mandatory explanation clause, not saturation and not an amplitude violation.

root_cause_fixed_this_round.was: the superseded anchor rule placed the mid-clip fingertip centroid on the box's top face, which with the clip's wrist pitch asks for a palm frame below the box top: the commanded hand sat -76 mm inside the box and the replay could only refuse it
root_cause_fixed_this_round.now: retarget/base_solve.py solves the floating base xyz against the box's grasp geometry (the 120 mm x span) with no hand geom interpenetration and a full pad-radius of palm-plate clearance; the closest fingertip approach is 0.03 mm from the box with 0.000 mm of penetration

palm_world_pose_deviation_mm.definition: ||palm_world(realised) - (hand_root + slide command)|| per control frame: how far the physics put the hand from the pose the solved command asked for

fingertip_world_pose_deviation_mm.note: the ring finger's base joint is commanded by the retargeter 0.93 rad outside its actuator range, and the constrained solve can only clip it; the clip's own fingertip layout therefore cannot be reproduced here

penetration.why: the fingertips now graze the box rather than driving into it: 0.000 mm against a 1 mm tolerance. The palm-vs-box stiffness hardening is still outstanding, so this number is contact on the pads only.

blocker.not_a_threshold_problem: PENETRATION_TOLERANCE_M, JOINT_VEL_LIMIT_RAD_S, WRIST_STEP_CEILING_M, the three signed velocity gates and both world-pose caps are all unchanged. Every gate added this round is sized from the frozen MJCF's own geometry (the box's 0.04 / 0.06 / 0.12 m half-dimensions) and from the measured servo behaviour, not from the observed result.

scene_side_evidence.note: measured on MJCF 4508421, frozen. These are the same scene smoke4 trains on, so every option below changes smoke4's physics too. The second block is smoke4's independent scan (240k random poses over 4 seeds plus a 52,020-pose wrist grid); it is reported here rather than re-derived, and the two agree on the mechanism.

smoke5_measurements.note: commanding ctrl_z from -0.163 up to -0.020 moves the wrist 1.1 mm: the bottom 60% of the wrist_z ctrlrange is saturated against the palm plate, which is what the old '0.869 m reachability floor' was

smoke4_measurements.palm_overload: the z position servo (kp 180 N/m, forcerange +-45 N) drives 26.4 N into a 1.47 N box -- an 18x overload, steady state
smoke4_measurements.pad_cannot_pass_own_finger: over poses where the box touches the hand, the median is 4 and the max 16 of the 16 finger collision geoms buried inside the box: the 12 mm pad sphere sits at the end of three phalanges and cannot reach the far 120 mm wall without going through its own finger, so every bilateral contact pose is an interpenetration and the solver ejects the box
smoke4_measurements.level_vs_below_top: the rotation that lowers pads below the box top (wrist_rx) spreads the three long fingers 47/65/78 mm apart in height at rx 0.6/0.9/1.2, so they rake the box; the rotation that keeps them level (wrist_rz, 0.0 mm spread) cannot lower them below the palm plate. The two cannot both be had.
smoke4_measurements.zero_undercut: the box bottom sits exactly on the pedestal top, so no finger can get beneath it
smoke4_measurements.search: 240k random poses over 4 seeds, a 52,020-pose structured wrist grid, and a 3,600-trial dynamic sweep (descend-then-close, close-then-descend, simultaneous; lift rates; curl amplitude): 0 clean trajectories. Pads-only contact occurs in ~1.3% of touching poses but never as an opposite-wall matched-height pinch.

scene_side_evidence.where_the_two_disagree: smoke4 reports the palm plate cannot be placed clear beside the box at all. This round's kinematic base solve does find a base with the plate 44.8 mm clear (palm frame at x=-0.104, y=+0.162), because the plate's 95 mm width runs along world x and the box's is only 120 mm wide. That does not rescue the grasp: in the physics the hand still ends up 86 mm from its own commanded pose and only 1 of 4 pads is within grasp radius. The kinematic clearance is real; the grasp is still not.

fixes_for_p1: scene-side, for Main's ruling (MJCF frozen at 4508421, smoke4 is training on it): raise the box on a short standoff so the palm can get beside and below it instead of over it, and/or narrow the grasp span below the palm plate's 95.2 mm. These are what the measurements above point at, not a wider wrist travel.
narrow the box's x span below ~95 mm: the pads physically cannot pass their own finger to reach the far wall of a 120 mm span, so no controller change can close a grasp across it on this scene.

the retargeter commands rfj0 0.93 rad outside its actuator range on every frame; that is a retargeting-vs-MJCF mismatch and it caps how well the clip's fingertip layout can be reproduced even once the grasp geometry exists.
palm-vs-box contact stiffness is not hardened yet, so the palm plate absorms 26.4 N while the gates report pad contact only.

the warm-start ramp commands exactly at the measured trackable hinge rate, and the servo's step response then overshoots it: the realised rate reaches 1.87 rad/s against the 1.5 rad/s cap. The cap is not the thing to change; the ramp should command below it by the measured overshoot factor.

gate_scope: G3 gates retarget *executability*: the MANO->Allegro sequence must be replayable through the scene's actuators with real finger-object contact, bounded motion and no interpenetration. It says nothing about hand-geometry accuracy, which stays inherited from HaMeR (smoke 6) and is recorded under fingertip_tracking.

wrist_reachability.interpretation: a non-empty axes_out_of_range means the retargeted wrist pose cannot be executed by this floating wrist; the replay then clips the command, so the executed trajectory differs from the retargeted one and the executed qpos is gated on the MJCF joint range instead

warm_start.unreachable_note: a DoF counted here holds a tracking error above the tolerance at the first commanded pose, which on this scene is sustained box contact: a finger in contact holds a contact-deflection error rather than the commanded value, and a wrist slide on the list means the commanded descent itself is outside the floating wrist's reachable set -- no approach path reaches it. The ramp caps the *command* rate; it cannot make an unreachable pose reachable.
warm_start.wrist_reachable_note: the commanded wrist pose is not HELD by this scene: on the superseded scenes the palm blocked the wrist's descent outright, on the W6a-v2 upright posture the servos saturate against gravity trying to hold it (wrist_rx demanded torque beyond its +-6 N m budget) and the pose sags. Either way no approach path makes the command stick -- the ramp caps the *command* rate; it cannot make an unholdable pose holdable.

rate_caps.source: free-space step/ramp measurement of this model's own servos (hinges 1.5 rad/s, wrist_y 0.2 m/s), tightened per axis to the servo's own derived winding allowance where the W6a re-scale put that below the measurement (x/z: 45 N / 280 = 0.1607 m/s); recorded in rerun_evidence.velocity_gate.floating_wrist_servo_ceiling

servo_winding_rate.rule: three-part servo winding tolerance, per wrist hinge: (1) realised rate <= |forcerange|/dof_damping, (2) at most 3 consecutive control intervals above that same cap, (3) every interval in which the servo outran the command-side trackable rate 1.5 rad/s has its excess over the commanded rate explained as this DoF's own wind-up release (release_j(t) = sqrt(kp_j * windup_j(t)^2 / (dof_M0_j + armature_j)), windup_j(t) = ctrl_j(t) - qpos_j(t)) with the actuator off its force limit. kv = 0 does not weaken the bound: dof_damping = 1.2 is what makes a finite bound exist at all. The bound is tight -- the free-space step asymptote of this servo plateaus at 4.90-4.97 rad/s (both directions, both step signs), within 2% of it; with dof_damping forced to 0 the plateau disappears entirely.

dv <= a_max * tau_s.rejected_because: an order of magnitude above the measured transient: forcerange/I ~ 94-98 rad/s^2 is the acceleration ceiling of a kp=14, I~0.062 wrist hinge, and tau_s = 0.2857 s is a window the command rate gives, not the servo.  A bound an order of magnitude above every achievable value gates nothing.

warm_start.tracking_error_note: finite by design: the first commanded pose puts the hand in sustained box contact, so the force-limited servos hold a contact deflection instead of reaching the commanded qpos exactly.
warm_start.velocity_scope: warm-start segment excluded from joint_velocity_max_rad_s by design: it is a rate-limited approach to the first command, not retargeted motion. Its own rates are below.

servo_winding_position.rule: three-part servo winding tolerance, per finger joint: (1) excess beyond jnt_range <= |forcerange|/kp, (2) at most 3 consecutive control frames (150 ms at 20 Hz), (3) the transient is elastic wind-up: there is a contact torque on that DoF, the actuator is not on its force limit while it happens, and kp*(ctrl-qpos) accounts for the whole non-actuator load on the DoF to 5%. An excursion during saturation is never exempted, and neither is one on a freely drifting joint.

gate_definition.measured_quantity: mean joint rate over one 20 Hz control period, np.diff(qpos)/0.05 -- an interval average, not the URDF's instantaneous max joint speed
gate_definition.applies_to_dofs_in_code: all 22 qpos DoFs, finger and wrist alike

urdf_velocity_scope.note: every velocity=3.14 attribute sits on a finger joint; the URDF's wrist_joint is type=fixed (the palm root), so the MJCF-only 6-DoF floating wrist has no URDF velocity specification to inherit.

startup_transient.note: reset_scene() seeds the wrist at identity, so interval 0 asks the servo for a step of up to ~1.3 rad in 50 ms. Intervals 1-2 are the servo still catching up to that step. The retargeted trajectory itself never asks for more than 2.05 rad/s after interval 2.

floating_wrist_servo_ceiling.measurement: box lifted 3 m clear in a throwaway model copy, so this is the servo alone and not a contact reaction
floating_wrist_servo_ceiling.tracking_criterion: mean achieved rate >= 0.9x the commanded rate
floating_wrist_servo_ceiling.conclusion: the servo peaks at 3.67 rad/s on a step but only tracks a constant-rate ramp faithfully up to 1.5 rad/s; 3.14 rad/s is a step-transient rate, not a 20 Hz trackable rate.

commanded_pose_probe.method: kinematic only (mj_forward, no dynamics, fingers at the reset pre-curl): box overlap of the commanded configuration
commanded_pose_probe.note: a ~53 mm burial would mean the gauge-fixed retarget output asks for fingers through the box. It does not: the commanded pose overlaps the box by well under a millimetre, so the deep-travel known boundary does not fire on this sequence.

box_contact_force_split.note: R1 sized forcerange for 10 N per fingertip, 40 N summed across the four pads; the peak per-frame total normal force on the box is reported for comparison. C6 counts any finger-or-palm geom, so a palm-only contact satisfies it; the per-geom breakdown records which geoms actually carry the load.
